title: When IBM Left India, a Cooking-Fat Maker Built a Computer
conflicts: Date of the move into computing: Stanford Magazine says 'late 1970s'; IISc records the consultancy agreement in July 1979 and Mitta's hiring in May 1980; the Economic Times timeline says Wipro entered IT in 1981 (product launch); an ICMR case summary seen in search claimed a first minicomputer in 1975 and was not used. The story gives each dated step. Company name spelling differs (Western India vs Western Indian Vegetable(s) Products); the story uses Stanford/IISc/Outlook India's 'Western India Vegetable Products'. No disagreeing outcome numbers were found; the story uses none beyond the Rs 14 lakh contract value.
notes: The 1966 shareholder-at-the-AGM detail rests on one source (Outlook India) and is attributed 'by one account'. 'Bootstrapped' reflects Premji's statement that the cooking-oil business funded the IT move; Wipro was already a listed company. IISc's own Connect article (502 error) and Quartz (403) could not be used.
